result_text:
## Summary
Compliance-audit SaaS (Vanta/Drata/Sprinto) and AI-governance/bias-audit platforms (Credo AI, Holistic AI) both sell almost entirely via custom sales-led quotes, priced on seats/models/frameworks, ranging roughly $10K-$120K+/yr for compliance automation and $30K-$200K+/yr (up to $500K-$1.5M/yr for large multi-hundred-model enterprise deployments, per analyst commentary) for AI governance platforms. MLOps/ML-observability open-core tools (Evidently AI, WhyLabs, Arize) instead give away a fully-featured OSS engine and monetize only the hosted/collaboration layer on a free→self-serve→enterprise ladder. BiasAperture's positioning (compliance/audit tool with a genuinely open, statistically rigorous core) maps best onto the open-core structural pattern for adoption, with the enterprise tier borrowing the AI-governance-platform sales-led custom-quote pattern. Proposed: (1) free open-core CLI, (2) paid hosted dashboard+API+CI tier, (3) custom-quote enterprise/audit-as-a-service tier.

## Comparable landscape

### A. Compliance-audit SaaS (SOC 2 / ISO / GRC automation)
- Vanta, Drata, Sprinto, Secureframe: none publish list prices; three recurring pricing archetypes across vendors — per-employee scaling (Vanta), flat platform fee + framework add-ons (Drata), and employee-band step tiers (Sprinto).
- Buyer-reported ranges: SMB single-framework ~$10K-$20K/yr; mid-market (50-200 employees) ~$25K-$55K/yr; enterprise multi-framework ~$80K-$120K+/yr. Each additional framework adds roughly $5K/yr on Vanta's model (discounted when bundled).
- Counter-model worth noting: episki publishes a flat $750/mo ($7,500/yr) covering unlimited users/frameworks/vendors, positioned explicitly against Vanta/Drata's opaque sales-led quotes — a viable differentiation angle if BiasAperture wants to compete on pricing transparency.

### B. AI-governance / bias-audit platforms (closest domain comparables)
- Credo AI: no published pricing; market-reported custom enterprise pricing $30,000-$150,000+/yr for ML-pipeline governance only, with estimated $40K-$200K+ total first-year cost including implementation/services for a mid-size buyer.
- Holistic AI: no published pricing either; sits in the same custom-enterprise-quote bracket as Credo AI.
- Broader AI-governance-platform (AIGP) market commentary (2026 buyer's guides) situates typical annual spend at roughly $25K-$200K+ depending on scope/pillars covered, with mid-market (50-100 models) first-year total cost of $200K-$400K and enterprise (200+ models) $500K-$1.5M cited by at least one vendor-adjacent guide — treat this upper band as directional analyst commentary, not a confirmed comparable.
- Structural pattern: essentially the entire AI-governance segment is sales-led/custom-quoted; nobody in this segment publishes self-serve tiers.

### C. MLOps / ML-observability open-core tools (packaging-model comparables — most transferable to BiasAperture)
- Evidently AI: core engine (100+ metrics, drift/quality/LLM eval) is fully free and open source (Apache 2.0) with **no feature gating on the engine itself**; Evidently Cloud adds a generous free tier plus paid self-serve/enterprise tiers for hosted dashboards, team collaboration, alerting, and (Enterprise only) onboarding/training — monetization lives entirely in the hosted layer, not the statistics. This is the closest structural analog to BiasAperture's own novelty-defense positioning (open, rigorous core engine as the trust signal).
- WhyLabs: same open-core shape — whylogs is free-forever OSS feeding a managed SaaS with a historically generous free tier and paid tiers billed on monitored data volume. Flag: sources conflict on WhyLabs' current commercial status — one source states WhyLabs Inc. discontinued commercial operations and open-sourced the full platform in 2026, another (dated later, less verifiable) describes an active paid tier at $0.50/10k inferences. Used here only for the packaging-pattern lesson, not as a live price point.
- Arize AI: free tier → Teams ~$500/mo → Enterprise custom — a clean three-rung self-serve-to-enterprise ladder.

## Proposed packaging for BiasAperture (3 tiers)

Mapped to Phase-2 capability tracks: Track 25 (Web Dashboard / Drill-Down Report UX), Track 31 (Config-Driven Audit-as-Code Profiles), and Track 32 (CI/CD commit-time gate — inferred from Track 31's coordination note referencing "Track 32's CI at commit-time"; Track 32's own task content wasn't independently available in shared team memory, so this attribution is inference, not confirmed). **Track 33 and Track 35 scope was not available in shared team memory at research time — not mapped to a tier below; their owners should confirm placement.**

### Tier 1 — Open-Core CLI (Free)
- The audit engine itself: dual-backend cross-validation, Core Four fairness metrics, n≥30 statistical discipline, bootstrap CI, regulatory-mapped report generation — fully usable locally via CLI, no feature gating.
- Modeled directly on Evidently AI / whylogs: give away the full statistical engine (the actual novelty-defense differentiator) to build adoption and credibility; monetize the layer above it, not the math itself.
- Target users: individual researchers, small teams running one-off/pre-launch audits, open-source credibility and community-building.

### Tier 2 — Hosted Dashboard + API (Paid, self-serve → sales-assisted)
- Adds: Track 25's hosted web dashboard / drill-down report UX, hosted API access, Track 31's config-driven Audit-as-Code profiles (overrides[] + approval audit-log workflow) for embedding audits in CI/CD, the inferred Track 32 CI/CD commit-time gate, and continuous/streaming audit mode (Track 21, CUSUM drift alerting).
- Pricing shape: follow the Evidently Cloud / Arize Teams pattern — generous free tier of the hosted layer, then self-serve usage- or seat-based paid pricing — rather than the fully-custom-sales-quote pattern used by Credo AI/Holistic AI. Publishing a self-serve price here is itself a differentiator against the AI-governance segment, where nobody publishes tiers.
- **Estimate, not a sourced comparable:** a plausible entry price in the ~$500-$2,000/mo range, bracketed loosely by Arize Teams (~$500/mo) and Evidently/WhyLabs paid-tier reports (~$300-$500/mo entry). This number is BiasAperture-specific reasoning, not drawn from a vendor's published rate — flagging explicitly per task instructions.

### Tier 3 — Enterprise / Audit-as-a-Service (Custom quote)
- Adds: on-prem/VPC deployment, a managed audit-as-a-service engagement model (BiasAperture team runs the audit + regulatory-mapping deliverable directly for the client), enterprise SSO/access control, custom regulatory-mapping packs beyond the default Core Four/EU AI Act mapping, SLA-backed support.
- Pricing shape: sales-led custom quote, following the Credo AI / Holistic AI / Vanta-Scale pattern — standard for this segment; no comparable in either adjacent market publishes self-serve enterprise pricing.
- **Sourced anchor:** Credo AI's market-reported $30,000-$150,000+/yr, consistent with the broader $25K-$200K+ AI-governance-platform bracket found across multiple independent 2026 market summaries. Use as a positioning anchor, not a commitment to match it exactly — BiasAperture's narrower audit/compliance scope (vs. Credo AI/Holistic AI's full governance-platform scope) is an argument for pricing toward the lower end of that band initially.

## Figures explicitly flagged as estimates vs. sourced comparables
- **Sourced (vendor/market-reported):** Credo AI $30K-$150K+/yr; Vanta/Drata/Sprinto SMB-to-enterprise $10K-$120K+/yr bands and per-framework ~$5K/yr add-on; Arize free→~$500/mo→enterprise; Evidently AI's fully-free/no-feature-gating OSS-engine-plus-paid-cloud structure; episki's flat $750/mo counter-model.
- **My own estimates, not sourced comparables:** the Tier 2 $500-$2,000/mo entry-price suggestion; using the $25K-$200K+ AI-governance bracket as Tier 3's anchor is a positioning choice, not a promise BiasAperture will land there.
- **Unverifiable/conflicting source:** WhyLabs' current commercial status (discontinued-and-open-sourced vs. still-active-with-paid-tier) — used only for the packaging-pattern lesson, not the specific price figure.

## Open items / coordination flags
- Track 33 and Track 35 capability scope wasn't visible in shared team memory at research time — tier mapping above covers Track 21/25/31/32 only; whoever owns 33/35 should confirm which tier(s) their capabilities belong to before this feeds the Phase-2 business case.
- Research-only task; no repo/code access was used or needed.
